system:
You are the research and qualification engine behind FlytBase's inbound sales desk. FlytBase sells an autonomy software platform that runs drones and drone docks (drone-in-a-box) at large industrial sites for inspection, security and emergency response, without pilots on site.
Task: write the positioning recommendation for this account, using ONLY the verified findings provided
(cite them by id). Stakeholders: list verified people from the findings (basis=verified, with finding ids) and,
separately, roles that are typically involved in such a purchase (basis=inferred_from_role, no names).
Never invent a person's name.

<qualification_gaps>
Metrics: Specific KPIs such as current annual spend on manual crews, frequency of inspections required, or safety incident targets.
Economic Buyer: Confirmation if Rodrigo has final sign-off authority or if the CFO/Division VP must approve the capital expenditure.
Decision Criteria: Technical specifications regarding data integration, connectivity requirements in remote areas, or specific sensor needs.
Decision Process: The steps following the budget conversation, such as technical validation (POC) or vendor comparison phases.
Paper Process: Procurement requirements, legal review timelines for international vendors, and Chile-specific tax or import documentation.
Champion: Confirmation that Rodrigo will actively advocate for FlytBase specifically against other internal priorities or competitors.
Competition: Whether they are looking at other drone-in-a-box providers or considering an internal drone program.
</qualification_gaps>
<verified_findings>
F01 [org_structure] SQM has established a new joint venture entity called Novandino Litio (also referred to as Nova Andino Litio) in partnership with the Chilean state-owned mining company CODELCO. (May 2026) — so what: This partnership represents a critical shift in how SQM's lithium operations are governed; autonomous drone solutions must align with the operational standards of both SQM and CODELCO.
F02 [org_structure] Carlos Díaz O. was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of Novandino Litio in June 2024, having previously served as VP of Operations for Potassium and Lithium. (June 2024) — so what: As the CEO of the specific entity managing the Atacama lithium partnership, Díaz is a primary stakeholder for high-level operational technology decisions like autonomous inspection.
F03 [org_structure] The Salar de Atacama mine is operated by the subsidiary Sociedad Química y Minera (SQM) Salar de Atacama S.A., which is owned by the parent company. (March 2026) — so what: Sales efforts for the Atacama Desert should target the leadership of this specific operating subsidiary while maintaining alignment with the parent company's executive suite.
F04 [org_structure] Pablo Altimiras C. serves as the CEO of the Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division, a role he assumed in June 2024 after leading the Lithium and Iodine businesses. (June 2024) — so what: Altimiras oversees a major industrial division that likely shares the same desert operating environment, offering a secondary entry point for drone-based inspection.
F05 [org_structure] Ricardo Ramos R. has served as the Chief Executive Officer of SQM since January 2019, following a long career in finance and corporate services within the company. (January 2019) — so what: The lead likely reports through a chain that terminates with Ramos; his long tenure suggests a preference for internal operational continuity and proven ROI.
F06 [org_structure] Felipe Smith is the executive heading the Lithium & Potassium division, which is currently SQM's largest revenue-generating segment. (2026) — so what: Smith is a key executive for the lead's division; autonomous drone operations that improve efficiency in this high-revenue segment will be highly prioritized.
F07 [org_structure] SQM's Board includes a Safety, Health and Environment Committee, which currently includes director Antonio Gil N. (April 2025) — so what: Autonomous drones directly support the mandate of this committee by removing personnel from hazardous desert environments, providing a safety-first justification for the purchase.
F08 [org_structure] The Salar de Atacama mine site employed 1,640 staff and 2,775 contractors as of mid-2025, highlighting a large workforce to manage in a remote area. (July 2025) — so what: The high ratio of contractors to employees suggests a complex organizational footprint where autonomous drones can provide consistent, standardized oversight without increasing headcount.
F09 [budget_signals] SQM projects a total capital expenditure of approximately US$3 billion for the three-year period spanning 2026 to 2028. (2026-2028) — so what: This massive budget allocation, particularly the 60% for Novandino, indicates significant capital available for technology that improves operational efficiency in the Atacama Desert.
F10 [budget_signals] The Salar Futuro project in the Salar de Atacama is estimated to require a US$3 billion capital investment over a seven-year development cycle. (July 2026) — so what: The long-term nature and high value of this project create a sustained opportunity for autonomous inspection solutions to support construction and ongoing monitoring.
F11 [budget_signals] SQM's investment plan for 2026-2028 includes approximately US$300 million per year dedicated to sustaining capital expenditures across all divisions. (2026-2028) — so what: A consistent US$300M annual maintenance budget provides a clear entry point for autonomous drones to replace manual, high-cost inspection and maintenance routines.
F12 [budget_signals] The Novandino joint venture plans to invest US$3 billion to increase lithium production by over 70%, targeting 470,000 metric tons annually. (July 2026) — so what: The scale of this expansion requires advanced site security and progress monitoring that autonomous drone docks are uniquely suited to provide in remote desert environments.
F13 [budget_signals] SQM has committed between US$450 million and US$500 million for the expansion of the Mt Holland lithium project. (July 2026) — so what: While this project is in Australia, it demonstrates SQM's willingness to commit large-scale Capex to international lithium expansion and infrastructure.
F14 [budget_signals] SQM's capital expenditures for the year ended December 31, 2025, reached US$876.7 million, focused on strategic expansion projects. (FY 2025) — so what: Historical spending patterns show a consistent near-billion-dollar annual investment in capacity, supporting the feasibility of high-value technology acquisitions.
F15 [budget_signals] SQM is investing in a seawater pipeline (TEA project) and leaching pile projects in María Elena as part of its Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division expansion. (FY 2025) — so what: Linear infrastructure like pipelines and large-scale leaching piles are ideal use cases for autonomous drone inspections to detect leaks or structural issues.
F16 [budget_signals] SQM's Board of Directors approved an interim dividend of US$1.43501 per share to be paid in September 2026. (August 2026) — so what: Strong dividend payouts indicate a healthy cash position, suggesting that budget for innovation is likely available despite high capital expenditure commitments.
F17 [news] SQM and Wesfarmers have approved a major expansion of the Mt Holland lithium project, which includes a new ore sorting facility and a second concentrator. (July 21, 2026) — so what: Expansion of physical infrastructure and ore sorting facilities increases the scale of operations requiring autonomous monitoring and inspection.
F18 [news] The Supreme Court of Chile has officially confirmed the validity of the joint venture between SQM and Codelco, rejecting legal appeals against the partnership. (January 26, 2026) — so what: The finalized partnership with Codelco (Nova Andino Litio) secures long-term operations in the Atacama, providing a stable environment for multi-year autonomous drone deployments.
F19 [news] SQM entered into a joint exploration agreement with Ivanhoe Electric Inc. in early 2026 to search for copper on its properties in northern Chile. (January 2026) — so what: New exploration projects in the Antofagasta region represent greenfield sites where autonomous drones can assist in mapping and site security without on-site pilots.
F20 [news] SQM's Board of Directors approved an interim dividend of US$1.43501 per share to be paid in September 2026. (August 25, 2026) — so what: Strong financial distributions indicate a healthy cash position, supporting capital expenditure for operational efficiency technologies like FlytBase.
F21 [news] Hernán Büchi Buc was appointed as the new Vice Chairman of SQM's Board of Directors following the resignation of Gonzalo Guerrero Yamamoto. (May 26, 2026) — so what: Changes in senior leadership can lead to shifts in strategic priorities regarding technology adoption and operational modernization.
F22 [news] SQM reported a significant increase in net income for the first half of 2026, reaching over $1 billion compared to $225.9 million in the same period of 2025. (First half of 2026) — so what: Dramatic profit growth provides the Northern Operations Division with the budget flexibility to invest in autonomous inspection platforms.
F23 [news] SQM produced 233,000 metric tons of lithium carbonate equivalent from its Atacama operations in 2025, maintaining its status as a low-cost producer. (Full year 2025) — so what: High production volumes at the Atacama site necessitate efficient, automated inspection to maintain the 'low-cost producer' advantage.
F24 [news] SQM has established an internal geological exploration team that has already identified more than 45 copper-prospective projects. (As of April 2026) — so what: The high volume of active exploration projects creates a demand for scalable, remote inspection solutions to monitor drilling targets across vast desert areas.
F25 [stakeholder_letters] SQM is prioritizing the validation of real-time plant-condition monitoring techniques using biosignal sensors. (2025) — so what: The focus on real-time monitoring aligns with FlytBase's capability to provide continuous, autonomous site surveillance and data collection.
F26 [stakeholder_letters] The company identifies operational slowdowns, stoppages, and delays caused by safety and environmental incidents as a significant risk factor. (2026-04-22) — so what: Autonomous drone docks can mitigate these risks by providing 24/7 safety monitoring and rapid emergency response without putting human pilots at risk.
F27 [stakeholder_letters] SQM's innovation strategy for the Salar de Atacama focuses on strengthening the value-generation chain and improving yields. (2025) — so what: FlytBase can support this innovation strategy by automating routine inspections of the value chain infrastructure in the remote desert environment.
F28 [stakeholder_letters] The company has completed conceptual engineering for 'Salar Futuro' to implement new technologies and improve water-use efficiency by 2030. (2025) — so what: As SQM designs future-state operations, FlytBase can be positioned as the standard platform for autonomous aerial data collection for these new technologies.
F29 [stakeholder_letters] SQM allocated over US$55 million in 2025 toward R&D, process improvement, and optimization initiatives. (2025) — so what: Significant R&D spending indicates a high budget for technological advancements, including autonomous systems that optimize mining processes.
F30 [stakeholder_letters] The Novandino Litio division is investing in support and sustainability initiatives, including environmental and regulatory compliance. (2025) — so what: Autonomous drones provide the consistent, auditable data required for environmental monitoring and regulatory compliance in sensitive areas like the Salar.
F31 [stakeholder_letters] SQM is focused on process improvement and optimization within its Iodine–Plant Nutrition Division. (2025) — so what: FlytBase can automate the inspection of iodine and nitrate processing plants to identify inefficiencies and support optimization goals.
F32 [stakeholder_letters] The Lithium Chemical Plant in Antofagasta is leveraging advanced technology to maintain its position as a cost leader with high recovery rates. (2025) — so what: Maintaining cost leadership in Antofagasta requires high operational efficiency, which autonomous drone inspections can enhance by reducing manual labor costs.

response.thesis: Position FlytBase as the operational standard for the Novandino Litio joint venture to manage the 70% production increase and US$3B 'Salar Futuro' expansion without increasing human risk or contractor headcount. By automating 24/7 inspections across the Atacama's remote lithium and iodine infrastructure, SQM can maintain its low-cost producer status while directly addressing the Safety, Health and Environment Committee's mandate to remove personnel from hazardous desert conditions.

value_hooks.hook: Automated Oversight for the Novandino Litio Expansion
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: With the Supreme Court confirming the Novandino partnership and a US$3B investment to increase lithium production by 70%, FlytBase provides the scalable, pilot-free infrastructure needed to monitor this massive expansion in the Atacama without a proportional increase in high-cost contractor crews.

value_hooks.hook: Safety-First Risk Mitigation for Remote Operations
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: Given that SQM identifies operational stoppages from safety incidents as a major risk, and currently manages over 2,700 contractors in remote areas, our autonomous docks remove humans from hazardous environments while providing 24/7 emergency response and safety monitoring.

value_hooks.hook: Optimizing Linear Infrastructure and Leaching Piles
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: For your Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division's new seawater pipelines and leaching pile projects, FlytBase enables real-time, autonomous detection of leaks and structural issues, directly supporting your 2025 innovation strategy to strengthen the value-generation chain.

likely_stakeholders.why_involved: CEO of Novandino Litio; primary decision-maker for technology adoption within the critical SQM-CODELCO lithium partnership.
Head of Lithium & Potassium division; oversees the highest revenue-generating segment where autonomous efficiency gains are most impactful.
Member of the Safety, Health and Environment Committee; interested in technologies that reduce personnel exposure to hazardous desert conditions.
CEO of Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division; relevant for drone applications in pipeline and leaching pile monitoring.
Likely required for final sign-off on capital expenditures related to the US$300M annual sustaining capital budget.
Responsible for validating real-time monitoring techniques and R&D-led process improvements.

risks_and_objections: Integration challenges with CODELCO's operational standards within the new Novandino joint venture.
Connectivity and hardware durability concerns in the extreme environment of the Atacama Desert.
Potential preference for internal R&D solutions given SQM's US$55M annual R&D spend.
Complex procurement and legal review timelines typical of Chilean state-partnered entities.
avoid: Avoid focusing solely on the Lithium division; the Iodine-Plant Nutrition division has specific linear infrastructure needs (pipelines) that are high-value use cases.
Do not ignore the influence of CODELCO's standards in the new joint venture entity.
Avoid suggesting solutions that require on-site pilots, as the primary pain point is the cost and hazard of personnel in remote areas.
